meta.title: The Store Doesn't Pay For 'Buy Now, Pay Later.' You Do, Just Not With Interest.
meta.hook: A four-payment checkout plan can feel free to the shopper because the merchant helps fund the system.
meta.description: Buy-now-pay-later apps like Affirm and Klarna make most of their money from merchant fees, not from you. Retailers pay these providers a cut of every sale, often around 6% plus a small flat fee, in exchange for a boost in checkout conversions and average order size. Late fees on missed payments are a secondary revenue source, not the main one. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Some plans charge late fees, and missed automatic payments can also trigger bank overdraft or insufficient-funds fees.

scenes.narration: So zero interest does not mean zero economics. The product shifts revenue toward merchant fees while keeping credit risk with the provider.
